newsitem.title: USA: Payless Cashways files for bankruptcy, to cut 1,900 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Payless Cashways files for bankruptcy, to cut 1,900 jobs.

text.p: Payless Cashways Inc., a building materials retailer, said Monday it has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection to restructure debt, and will close 29 stores and cut 1,900 jobs.
About 100 of the jobs will be at the company's Kansas City, Mo., headquarters and regional administrative centres.

Payless operates 194 building materials stores under the names of Payless Cashways, Furrow, Lumberjack, Hugh M. Woods, Somerville Lumber, Knox Lumber, and Contractor Supply in 22 states in the Midwestern, Southwestern, Pacific Coast, Rocky Mountain and New England areas. It has 17,000 employees.
Payless said the filing follows negotiations with its senior lenders over the past several weeks in an attempt to restructure its heavy debt.

"After considering all other alternatives, including the sale of the company and liquidation, it became clear that Chapter 11 provided the best approach for a comprehensive restructuring of the company," Chairman David Stanley said in a statement.
"Our plan will finally create a capital structure to support the operation of our business after a decade of dealing with a highly leveraged balance sheet," he said.
Payless said a group of financial institutions led by Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, the company's agent bank, has agreed to provide $125 million in financing.
The company has also secured a commitment for $150 million of financing from a group of lenders for use after it emerges from bankruptcy.
The financing, which is subject to court approval, is expected to provide adequate funding for all trade and employee obligations, as well as operating needs during the restructuring, Payless said.

Although Payless was profitable on a pretax basis in its second quarter ended May 31 and had sufficient liquidity to fund current operations, Stanley said the company was unlikely to meet the requirements of its principal credit agreements at the end of the current fiscal year.

The Chapter 11 petition will allow Payless to operate its business without interruption while it obtains necessary approval of its reorganization plan from the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of Missouri in Kansas City, it said.
Payless' stock closed Friday at 62.5 cents on the New York Stock Exchange.
